_source: Measured values. Cross-validation and feature importance from src/train_hotspot_model.py; independent validation from src/enrich_and_validate.py (ties broken at random, mean of 200 draws).
unit_of_analysis: one 0.05 degree cell (~5 km), not one detection

independent_validation.ground_truth: WRI Global Power Plant Database (11,199 thermal plants)
independent_validation.note: This dataset was never a feature and never a label, so it is a genuinely independent test.

feature_importance.method: Permutation importance on a held-out spatial fold, scored by average precision

limitations.title: Finds persistent heat, not confirmed factories
limitations.body: The model scores how steadily a place burns. It cannot tell a gas flare from a smelter, a brick kiln or a geothermal vent.

limitations.title: 16% confirmation does not disprove the rest
limitations.body: Only 16% of High alerts match a known thermal power plant. The reference database lists power plants, not flares or kilns, so absence from it is not evidence against a site.

limitations.title: It does not predict future fires
limitations.body: Everything here is measured from observations the satellite already made. Forecasting where a fire will start needs weather, fuel dryness and vegetation data this system does not use.

limitations.title: Training labels come from NASA's own classification
limitations.body: The model learns from the FIRMS type field, which is a useful clue rather than audited ground truth. The independent power-plant check exists precisely because of this.

superseded.note: An earlier detection-level model reported 0.989 ROC-AUC. That number was inflated: latitude alone scored 0.922 because the model had memorised where oil fields are, and a random train/test split let the same flare appear in both halves. Do not quote it.
